 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli

The present appeal preferred by the claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeks to assail the award dated 23.12.2017 passed by the learned MACT insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned.

Vide the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has, while awarding a total compensation of Rs.5,91,500/- alongwith interest @ 9% per annum to the appellant, awarded a sum of Rs.51,324/- towards the loss of income for six months due to the accident injury.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this loss of income for the period of six months was determined by the learned Tribunal by taking into account the minimum wages of an unskilled worker instead of taking the actual income of the appellant.

He, however, concedes that Income Tax Returns (ITRs) for the relevant period were not filed before the learned Tribunal by the appellant and the same have been placed on record for the first time with the present appeal.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the appellant having chosen not to file his ITRs before the learned Tribunal, cannot now be permitted to urge that the loss of income for the period of six months should have been calculated on the basis of these ITRs.

4. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, even though I find merit in the submission of learned counsel for the respondent that it is the appellant himself who failed to Mohd Israil vs Yogender Singh & Ors(United India ... on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26249697/
1 produce the relevant ITRs before the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: However, taking into account that the appellant is entitled to receive fair and just compensation and the appellant's ITRs which are now sought to be brought on record are public documents
, I am of the view that it will be in the interest of justice that the appellant should be given an opportunity to prove these ITRs.
The matter should therefore, be reconsidered by the learned Tribunal after granting an opportunity to the appellant to produce his ITRs before the learned Tribunal as per law.

5. For the aforesaid reasons, the impugned award insofar as it relates to grant of Rs. 51,324/-
towards the loss of income for six months due to the injuries suffered on account of the accident is set aside.

The matter is remanded back to the learned Tribunal for re-determination of compensation under this head of 'Loss of Income'.
6.

The matter will be listed before the learned Tribunal on 20.04.2023 and a fresh award will be passed in accordance with law after granting an opportunity to the appellant to produce his ITRs in evidence.
7. The appeal stands disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
